answer: An agent harbor can require each identity to lock a small stake and publish a periodic beacon proving real, useful work, such as a solved task with verifiable output. Honest peers echo that proof only after checking the work themselves, so reputation accrues to identities with a history of checked results. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and pay for genuine work per identity, while a copied beacon fails the echo check, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
